profile.name: Zhezhi
profile.introduction: Zhezhi is a commissioned painter, quiet and shy with a dedication to her craft. She's not very eloquent, but her persistence and love for painting speak volumes.
profile.review:
Zhezhi is a 5-star Glacio Rectifier Hybrid who focuses on buffing Glacio and Resonance Skill damage while having the aptitude to do off-field damage. Specializing in relatively quick on-field combos followed by off-field Coordinated Attacks, she will provide constant damage support both when she’s on and when she’s off the field, able to not only buff your characters but also provide a decent source of on and off-field single-target damage. This defines her core use cases and playstyle.

Key Mechanics

All of Zhezhi’s gameplay revolves around her Forte gauge, which allows her to accumulate up to 3 stacks called Afflatus. Generated through her Intro Skill and Basic Attacks, her Forte gauge has 3 segments for a total of 90 Afflatus points, 30 points per stack.

Once a segment is full, Zhezhi can convert it into a Phantasmic Imprint using specific abilities. These Phantasmic Imprints are teleport points visible on the field that Zhezhi will teleport to and deal damage with, while generating a lot of Concerto Energy when she uses her Resonance Skill with Phantasmic Imprints placed and ready to activate on the field.

She can convert the segments in two ways: using her base Resonance Skill, which can convert up to 2 segments, and her Forte Heavy Attack (which can be triggered immediately by performing a Basic Attack after her Resonance Skill), which can convert the last segment when her Forte gauge is full. In case she gets interrupted on that attack however, she may cast it via a Heavy following a teleport Skill as well, provided she has enough Forte to consume.

With all of the above information, Zhezhi’s rotation becomes clear: She may rotate by activating her Intro skill, filling 1.5 segments of her Forte gauge, then completing a full Basic Attack sequence, filling out the remaining 1.5 segments, using her Resonance Skill and Forte Heavy Attack to convert them all into Imprints, which she will teleport to in quick succession, finishing with her Echo before finally being able to give her 20% Glacio, 25% Skill DMG Amplify Outro to the Main DPS to boost their damage. Her Outro skill has the additional effect of restoring Resonance Energy to the character you switch into - something that is very desired on both DPS characters she typically supports, Carlotta and Jinhsi.

The gameplay she sports looks fundamentally extremely simplistic - and that statement describes how Zhezhi plays out very accurately. Her ease of use is one of her big selling points, and the above sequence of actions is easy to remember and execute while being quite fast and close to optimal (though it can be optimized via Jump Cancels).

From a meta standpoint, Zhezhi is nowadays powercrept because she supports powercrept damage dealers. Resonance Skill amplifiers are scarce and the alternatives are bottom tiers in the form of Lumi and Taoqi, but general buffers like Lynae overtake Zhezhi’s spot on most teams outside of her unique use case with Jinhsi since she necessitates Coordinated Attacks. Her ease of use and rare Resonance Skill damage buffing ability make her a strong contender for Jinhsi and Carlotta, but those DPS characters have long since been overshadowed by more recent ones, like Luuk and Hiyuki in the same elements for example.

In conclusion, even though Zhezhi is one of the very rare choices for Glacio & Skill damage dealers, a lack of something that makes her stand out like strong personal damage, a lightning fast rotation time or high buffing potential make her an overshadowed buffer for DPS characters who are long since
profile.pros:
• Has one of the strongest off-field damage outputs in the game (barring full-fledged off-field Main DPS characters like Phrolova).

  • Very quick rotation that can be easily improved via Jump Cancels for solid damage and good buffs.

  • Very accessible weapon options, not Signature reliant at all.

  • Super consistent - attacks from a very far range and teleports around, almost never gets hit by enemies after her Basic chain and first Skill/Heavy Attack cast.

  • Provides extra Energy to the incoming character via her Inherent Skill on Outro, making Energy requirements easier to meet.
profile.cons:
• Lower damage ceiling overall compared to modern Hybrid characters, and generally lower, more niche buffing profile - easily replaced and outclassed in all teams barring Jinhsi, who is long since powercrept (in a very direct manner too by Luuk Herssen who Zhezhi does not work with).

  • Low headroom for quickswap; her only quickswap window is during her Basic 3.

  • Like most version 1 characters, has terrible sequence scaling, meaning they really aren’t worthwhile pickups.

  • Moonlit Clouds can be awkward to use by nature of Impermanence Heron being a Transform Echo, making her default to Empyrean Anthem for comfort where high stats are a necessity for the set to be worth it.

profile.rotations:
Zhezhi’s primary rotation goal is to fill her Forte gauge to then cast her Skill, Heavy Attack, finally teleport with her Skill 3 times, and Outro. She is free to cast her Ultimate at any point in this rotation.

Echo timing

Right before Outro (for Moonlit + Impermanence Heron, may require a Dash Cancel on the last Creation’s Zenith Skill), or at any point in the rotation (for Empyrean Anthem + Nightmare: Lampylumen Myriad).

Standard Rotation

  • Intro

  • Basic 1

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Skill

  • Heavy: Conjuration

  • Skill: Stroke of Genius (Jump Cancel)

  • Skill: Stroke of Genius (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Skill: Creation’s Zenith (Dash cancel into Echo, Swap, Outro on Moonlit Clouds OR Swap and Outro on Empyrean Anthem)

  • Outro

Possible Optimizations & No Ultimate Rotation

Without Ultimate available, an extra Basic 123 into Skill (Swap) before Outro may be necessary in order to get Zhezhi’s Outro properly. This is necessary in later rotations of Jinhsi + Zhezhi teams, but will not see use in Carlotta teams.

Finally, Zhezhi’s only further optimizations than what we listed above, can be to use her Ultimate as early as possible in Jinhsi teams (this means another Jump Cancel will need to be timed properly on the second Skill cast otherwise Zhezhi will be sent flying up into the air and lose time which makes it riskier), and her Basic 123 chain can be cast before Intro and Basic 3 can be Swap Cancelled to save more time as well (this allows Zhezhi to Intro and cast her Skill immediately afterwards, making the rotation more consistent and saving time overall).

Lastly, on Moonlit Clouds, her Echo may be cast before her rotation starts if you have that much headroom for Swap Cancels available (generally not realistic in Carlotta and Jinhsi team rotations beyond the Opener rotation however).

skills.name: Dimming Brush
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Glacio DMG.

Heavy Attack

Consume STA to perform an attack, dealing Glacio DMG.

Heavy Attack does not reset the Basic Attack cycle.

Mid-air Attack

Consume STA to perform up to 2 consecutive attacks while in mid-air, dealing Glacio DMG.

Dodge Counter

Use Basic Attack after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Glacio DMG.

skills.name: Manifestation
skills.description:
Deal Glacio DMG. If Afflatus is no less than 60, consume 60 Afflatus to summon Phantasmic Imprint - Left and Phantasmic Imprint - Right.

  • Press the button on the ground to summon the Phantasmic Imprints on the ground.

  • Hold the button on the ground or press the button in mid-air to summon the Phantasmic Imprints in mid-air.

skills.name: Living Canvas
skills.description:
Summon Inklit Spirits for assistance.

Can be cast in mid-air.

Inklit Spirit

When the active Resonator deals DMG, an Inklit Spirit will be summoned to perform a Coordinated Attack, dealing Glacio DMG, considered as Basic Attack DMG.

  • For 3s after dealing DMG, 1 Inklit Spirit is summoned per second. This effect can trigger once per second. Damage dealt by an Inklit Spirit does not trigger this effect.

  • Up to 1 Inklit Spirit can be summoned every second, and up to 21 in total.

  • This effect lasts for 30s, or until max Inklit Spirits are summoned.

skills.name: Ink and Wash
skills.description:
Phantasmic Imprint

Zhezhi may summon Phantasmic Imprints at the cost of Afflatus when casting Resonance Skill Manifestation or Heavy Attack Conjuration.

Up to 1 of each of Phantasmic Imprint - Left, Phantasmic Imprint - Middle, and Phantasmic Imprint - Right can exist at the same time, each lasting for 15s.

Heavy Attack: Conjuration

The 5 moves below consume STA to perform Conjuration to attack the target, dealing Glacio DMG.

  • Hold the Normal Attack button shortly after Basic Attack Stage 3.

  • Press the Normal Attack button shortly after casting Resonance Skill Manifestation.

  • Hold the Normal Attack button shortly after casting Resonance Skill Stroke of Genius or Resonance Skill Creation's Zenith.

  • Hold the Normal Attack button while in mid-air.

  • Hold the Normal Attack button after a successful Dodge.

If Zhezhi has at least 30 Afflatus when performing any of these, consume 30 Afflatus to summon a Phantasmic Imprint - Middle.

Resonance Skill: Stroke of Genius

When a Phatasmic Imprint is nearby, the Resonance Skill is replaced with Stroke of Genius, which can be cast while in mid-air. When it is cast, Zhezhi will:

  • Move to the location of the Phatasmic Imprint, remove it, and then summon an Ivory Herald to attack the target, dealing Glacio DMG, considered as Basic Attack DMG. Refresh the mid-air Dodge attempts if the target Phatasmic Imprint is in mid-air.

  • Gain 1 stack of Painter's Delight, lasting for 8s and stacking up to 2 times.

Resonance Skill: Creation's Zenith

When a Phantasmic Imprint is nearby and there are 2 stacks of Painter's Delight, Stroke of Genius is replaced with Creation's Zenith, which can be cast while in mid-air. When it is cast, Zhezhi will:

  • Lose all stacks of Painter's Delight

  • Move to the location of the Phantasmic Imprint, remove it, and then summon an Ivory Herald to attack the target, dealing greater Glacio DMG, considered as Basic Attack DMG, additionally increasing the Basic Attack DMG Bonus by 18% for 27s. Refresh the mid-air Dodge attempts if the target Phatasmic Imprint is in mid-air.

Afflatus

  • Zhezhi can hold up to 90 Afflatus.

  • Normal Attacks grant Afflatus on hit.

  • Casting Intro Skill grants Afflatus.

profile.calculationsNotes: Important! In the Sequence calculations below we have assumed you'll be fightning enemies for at least 2 or more Zhezhi rotations and will be able to maintain and refresh her buffs that last for 27 - 30 seconds at a time without letting them expire. For shorter fights or if you're not confident keeping buffs active you can consider Sequence 1, 3 and 4 to be less valuable than is displayed as they'll have lower uptime for you than we assume.

weapons.Comment: Zhezhi's Signature and best weapon gives her significant ATK and CRIT DMG stat boosts as well as a scaling Basic DMG Bonus buff that particularly affects her off-field Coordinated Attacks, perfectly synergizing with her kit and giving her the highest damage output she can get.
Cantarella's Signature also gives Zhezhi a very high Basic DMG Bonus buff and the same base stats as her Signature, making it a near-equal alternative to her Signature weapon.

Phrolova's Signature stands out as the only Rectifier with high Base ATK which works well on Zhezhi, not to mention the easily triggered Echo and Skill DMG Amplification as well as the DEF Ignore for 12s, all of which gives her a nice damage boost overall.

Yinlin's Signature Rectifier is easily one of the best generalist options in the game, giving Zhezhi a nice but short-lived ATK% buff that can apply to some Coordinated Attacks and the most damaging part of her on-field rotation. However, buffs run out quickly which make it not as ideal as her Signature while still being a completely excellent replacement.
Calculation also applicable to Luminous Hymn. Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Zhezhi, who does not benefit from this weapon's Fusion Burst and Tune Strain-oriented effects.

Best permanently available option for all Rectifier damage dealers, granting a scaling Basic DMG Bonus buff, some Energy Regen and a massive amount of ATK. Not as ideal as above options due to the absence of CRIT in the stats this weapon grants, but still a capable alternative.

Best 4-star weapon option, this Battle Pass Exclusive gets an easy-to-activate ATK buff when casting Ultimate and also gives a nice CRIT secondary stat but has lower Base ATK as a 4-star making it worse than any 5-star option.

Another good Battle Pass Exclusive that grants ATK and Basic DMG when casting Skill, not as ideal as any 5-star due to low Base ATK but also gives CRIT DMG on its secondary stat, making it a decent choice overall albeit easily replaced.
Grants some flat Energy when casting Skill and otherwise only gives some decent ATK increases. Replace this weapon when possible, but decent placeholder until 5-star options are acquired.
Similarly to Fusion Accretion, best no-gacha option accessible at the start of the game but gives nothing except ATK and should be replaced as soon as possible.

echoes.Comment: Offers an unconditional 10% Energy Regen% and 80% Coordinated DMG boost. Also grants a passive supportive effect which triggers when the wearer of this set critically strikes with a Coordinated attack - this effect grants the on field Resonator an ATK% boost regardless if they're the wearer of the set or not. The set is better than Moonlit Clouds if and only if the equipped character's Echoes have endgame investment (with 9 or 10 CRIT substats total) and the character has a 5-star weapon equipped. If both conditions aren't met, Moonlit Clouds is a better choice.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: The best Echo for Zhezhi when running the Empyrean Anthem set as it grants her an extra Glacio and Coordinated Attack DMG boost when equipped in the main slot, without taking up rotation time as it is a simple Summon Echo.

echoes.Comment: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

echoStats.Name: zhezhi
echoStats.Substats: Energy Regen (Until Satisfied) > CRIT Rate = CRIT DMG > ATK% > Basic DMG% > Flat ATK

skillPriority.Order: Res. Liberation, Forte Circuit, Basic Attack, Res. Skill, Intro Skill
skillPriority.Comments: Basic, Skill and Intro can be skipped when levelling to save on resources at a minimal damage loss.

teams.Name: Best Team
teams.Comments: Verina can be equal to Shorekeeper in Jinhsi teams with enough crit-fishing (particularly with S2 Verina). Other options under specific circumstances may include Hiyuki+Chisa, or Mornye as a general Support at S1 and above (or R4 Discord and above as a Verina alternative).

synergies.Comment: These are the DPS choices where Zhezhi is most valuable. While she can function as a Hybrid for teams like Hiyuki+Chisa to buff Hiyuki's Glacio DMG for example, Zhezhi shines at her best in teams that can fully utilize her Outro skill or benefit from her Coordinated Attacks. Her DPS of choice to pair with since version 2.0 has been Carlotta, who utilizes her entire array of buffs to the fullest; but since her release, she's also been Jinhsi's best partner by virtue of being the only Coordinated Attacker who rotates fast without the need for her Ultimate to complete a rotation, while amplifying Skill DMG. Lingyang is also acceptable as a fallback option if the team is built well and Lingyang's optimal playstyle is mastered - in those situations, it may suffice to clear endgame content.

Since Zhezhi is a generalist Glacio/Skill Amplifier and Coordinated Attack secondary damage dealer, she works best with Supports that increase damage generally, Shorekeeper and Verina being the two best generalists in the game to date as later Support releases got more and more specialized.
